title: Derivitization of polyphosphate with cystamine for biotin labeling
author: Catherine J. Baker
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7z3hp8n
materials: Prepare and combine all materials in this order to a 1.5, 2 or 5 mL tube. At the last minute, dissolve dry EDAC powder in water to make a 2 M solution. Then add to reaction. NOTE: EDAC is very hydroscopic and will degrade with exposure to humidity. Store powder aliquots of EDAC at -20 °C, dessicated. For each reaction, remove aliquot from freezer, allow to warm to room temperature. Refrain from dissolving until immediately before use. Do not store dissolved EDAC.

steps.title: Reduce polyP with TCEP
steps.instruction: Prepare a 100 mM TCEP stock by dissolving 5.5 mg TCEP in 191 µL water. Add 50 µL of this stock to 1000 µL polyP reaction solution to reach a final TCEP concentration of 5 mM. Immediately incubate at 37 °C for 1 h, agitating occasionally.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 5.5 mg TCEP in 191 µL water (100 mM stock).
Add 50 µL of the stock to 1000 µL polyP solution (final 5 mM).

steps.title: Remove condensation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube briefly to collect any condensation from the top of the tube.

steps.title: Desalt and exchange buffer (remove cystamine)
steps.instruction: Apply the sample to a 5 mL Zeba™ Spin Desalting Column (7 kDa MWCO) and follow the manufacturer’s protocol, eluting into 20 mM Hepes‑NaOH, pH 7.4, containing 5 mM EDTA to remove excess cystamine and prepare for the maleimide reaction.

steps.title: Quantify phosphate by malachite green
steps.instruction: Take an aliquot of the desalted sample and determine phosphate concentration using a malachite green assay, preparing standards in the same 20 mM Hepes‑NaOH pH 7.4 + 5 mM EDTA buffer.

steps.title: Estimate labeling degree
steps.instruction: Calculate the approximate biotin‑to‑polyP‑end ratio using the phosphate concentration (from malachite green) and biotin quantitation, assuming the mode polymer length; note that ratios >10 may indicate incomplete purification.

steps.title: Incubate polyP‑cystamine mixture
steps.instruction: Rotate the tube at room temperature for 1.5 h.

steps.title: Desalt to remove TCEP
steps.instruction: Run the reaction through a 5 mL Zeba™ Spin Desalting Column (7 kDa MWCO) and exchange into 20 mM Hepes‑NaOH, pH 7.4, + 5 mM EDTA to eliminate residual TCEP.

steps.title: Prepare maleimide‑biotin stock and react
steps.instruction: Dissolve 6.5 mg maleimide‑biotin in 50 µL water to make a 250 mM stock. Add 32 µL of this stock to 1000 µL of the purified, reduced polyP‑cystamine sample, yielding an 8 mM maleimide‑biotin concentration.

substeps.instruction: Make 250 mM maleimide‑biotin stock (6.5 mg in 50 µL water).
Add 32 µL of stock to 1000 µL polyP‑cystamine sample (final 8 mM).

steps.title: Optional biotin quantification
steps.instruction: If desired, measure biotin concentration using the Pierce Fluorescence Biotin Quantitation Kit according to the kit instructions.

steps.title: Conjugation incubation
steps.instruction: Vortex the reaction briefly, then rotate at room temperature for 1.5 h.

steps.title: Final desalting to remove excess biotin
steps.instruction: Desalt the reaction using a 5 mL Zeba™ Spin Desalting Column (7 kDa MWCO), eluting into 20 mM Hepes‑NaOH, pH 7.4, + 5 mM EDTA. This buffer may be changed for downstream applications; for EDAC‑labeled polyP, store in a buffer pH 7–8 with at least 100 µM EDTA to chelate trace metals.
